_readme: Product findings surfaced by this suite, rendered into reports/api-report.html.
Hand-written: a finding lands here once someone has judged it. `status` says how far:
confirmed    reproduced, and the behaviour is agreed to be wrong
intermittent real, but does not reproduce on demand
unconfirmed  observed; could still be test data or a wrong expectation
not-a-bug    kept because it was reported once and ruled out
`evidence` should name the case that shows it, so a reader can find the request below.

findings.title: every eRFX event save and publish fails with 500
findings.detail: Both status "draft" and status "active" return 500 Internal Server Error. A regression: the same automation published successfully at 07:49 on 2026-09-08 and has failed since ~16:29 that day. Non-eRFX single-stage creation still works, so the seven eRFX journeys reach publish and stop there.

findings.title: event-group create accepts invalid payloads with 200
findings.detail: A negative quantity, a non-numeric quantity and an unrecognised unit symbol are all accepted and persisted. Type and range enforcement happens client-side only, so any caller that is not the UI can write nonsense into a tender.
findings.evidence: [negative] a negative quantity is refused / text in the numeric quantity field is refused / an unrecognised quantity unit is refused

findings.title: invalid input returns 500 instead of a client error
findings.detail: An unknown product uuid, an unknown status value, and status "active" at create time each return 500 rather than 4xx. Invalid input reaching a 500 means it got past validation into code that assumed it had resolved, and a 500 leaks framework detail to the caller.
findings.evidence: [negative] a line item naming a product that does not exist is refused / an unknown status value is refused / an event cannot be created already active

findings.title: vendor evaluation fails with "Insufficient parameters"
findings.detail: runEvaluation returns 422 "Insufficient parameters" on some runs and passes on others, from an identical journey. Either the payload is missing a field the API only sometimes requires, or it depends on state left by an earlier step.

findings.title: a JSON body sent as text/plain is accepted
findings.detail: Content-Type is ignored and the body parsed as JSON regardless. Defensible, since many APIs do this deliberately, so recorded as behaviour to know rather than a defect to fix.
findings.evidence: [edge] a JSON body sent as text/plain gets a deliberate answer
